newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU flour exports still rising but pace slows.
newsitem.headline: EU flour exports still rising but pace slows.

text.p: Soft wheat flour export commitments from the European Union rose again in the week to February 25, but the pace of the increase fell sharply as lower refunds kicked in, EU figures circulated on Monday showed.
Export commitments rose 83,000 tonnes to bring the total since the season began on July 1 last year to 4.736 million tonnes, according to data supplied by member country officials.
In the previous week, the amount committed for export jumped by 749,000 tonnes after the EU granted a large block of licences to export more than 600,000 tonnes.
In February the EU cut its standing export refund for the main class of soft wheat flour -- first from 26 Ecus to 24.5 Ecus per tonne, and then to 20 Ecus and finally 17 Ecus.

Export commitments for soft wheat commercial grain exports between July 1, 1996, and February 25 this year reached 7.312 million tonnes. Those for barley grain reached 4.401 million tonnes, the latest compilation showed.
Total export licence awards for grain and grain products in the same period reached 21.211 million tonnes, up 47 percent from the same period in the previous season.
The figures were distributed to EU member states at weekly grain talks in Brussels on February 27.
All figures are drawn up on a grain-equivalent basis.
